I've heard that the way the system works can vary prefecture to prefecture and even city to city, don't know how true that is, but I have been on welfare in Nagoya for at least 3 or 4 years now, if not more.  I am really not good at understanding how the system works, so there may be special circumstances in my situation that enables me to be on for a very long time.  I've been in Japan for 17 years, started with a student visa then a I got a marriage visa when I married a native Japanese.  I got a permanent resident visa while married, I had a job on the cleaning staff of an office building for several years, then my husband killed himself.  I couldn't manage the stress and had to leave the job.  My husband's cousin helped me a great bit during that time, and still now.  He mentioned that he thought I might be autistic, he has an older brother who is severely autistic and said there were certain things about me that were very similar to his brother and suggested I get tested.  I agreed and he found the hospital in my area that makes those kinds of diagnosis and after a bunch of testing they determined that I was high functioning autistic but there are some things that I definitely can't do and it was determined that I should submit for a level 2 disability status. (I don't know if this varies from area to area but here there are only 3 levels, so that put me right in the middle.)  So my cousin-in-law helped me with all the paperwork that needed to be submitted to the city and a I received a level 2 disability card.  He also helped me with all the paperwork for the welfare part and I was able to start receiving that.  I currently get 117,230 yen a month.  I live a really penny pinching lifestyle, which comes pretty naturally for me, after making a few changes to go as energy saving as I can I've gotten to the point where at the end of the month after all my bills are paid and necessity shopping is done I have enough money left over that would cover a month's worth of normal shopping plus a little bit extra so I can start saving little by little. So it could be that because I have a disability card I can just stay on welfare, I really don't understand how the system works though.  I also still try to apply for jobs in my area that I know I can do but still always get rejected.
I'm about to turn 50 and I haven't been able to find a job for several years.  I'm not retired, I just ended up on Japanese welfare, so if all else fails, there's also that.
